quests.title: Pudding Lane Blaze
quests.story: Sparks are flying on Pudding Lane! Help the people of London understand the fire that changed their city.
quests.instruction: Read each question about the fire, then tap the right answer.
quests.hint: Think about London in 1666: wooden houses, narrow streets and no fire engines.

questions.ask: Which street did the Great Fire start in?
questions.fact: Pudding Lane was a narrow street near London Bridge.

questions.ask: What kind of shop did the fire start in?
questions.fact: It began in Thomas Farriner's bakery, where the oven fire had not been put out.

questions.ask: In what year was the Great Fire?
questions.fact: The fire began early on Sunday 2 September 1666.

questions.ask: Who was king at the time?
questions.fact: King Charles II helped the firefighters by passing buckets of water himself.

questions.ask: What were most houses made of?
questions.fact: Wooden houses were packed close together, so flames jumped easily from one to the next.

questions.ask: What blew the flames across the city?
questions.fact: The summer had been hot and dry, and a strong east wind fanned the fire.

questions.ask: How long did the fire burn?
questions.fact: The fire started on a Sunday and was almost out by the Thursday.

questions.ask: Which great church burned down?
questions.fact: The heat was so great that lead from the roof ran down the streets like a river.

questions.ask: Who wrote a famous diary about the fire?
questions.fact: Pepys wrote down what he saw each day, so we know a lot about the fire.

questions.ask: About how many houses burned down?
questions.fact: Around 13,200 houses and 87 churches were lost, and many people had no home.

questions.ask: Which river did people escape on?
questions.fact: People piled their things into boats on the River Thames to get away.

questions.ask: What tall column helps us remember the fire?
questions.fact: The Monument is 61 metres tall, the same as its distance from where the fire began.

quests.title: Firefighters Then and Now
quests.story: The fire is spreading! Some ways to fight it are from 1666, and some are from today. Can you sort them?
quests.instruction: Is it from 1666, or from today? Tap the right basket.
quests.hint: Does it need electricity, an engine or a phone? None of those existed in 1666.

questions.ask: Leather buckets of water
questions.fact: People stood in a long line, passing buckets from the river to the fire.

questions.ask: Long hooks to pull down houses
questions.fact: Pulling houses down made a gap, so the fire had nothing more to burn.

questions.ask: A hand squirt
questions.fact: A squirt was like a giant syringe that held only a few litres of water.

questions.ask: Church bells ringing as a warning
questions.fact: Bells were rung backwards, from the lowest note up, to warn of a fire.

questions.ask: Gunpowder to make fire breaks
questions.fact: Soldiers blew up some houses to make big gaps that the fire could not cross.

questions.ask: Saving things by burying them
questions.fact: Samuel Pepys buried his wine and his Parmesan cheese in his garden!

questions.ask: A fire engine with a siren
questions.fact: Fire engines carry ladders, hoses and their own tank of water.

questions.ask: A smoke alarm in the house
questions.fact: A smoke alarm beeps loudly to wake people up if there is smoke at night.

questions.ask: Calling 999
questions.fact: The 999 number began in London in 1937, the first of its kind in the world.

questions.ask: A breathing mask and air tank
questions.fact: Firefighters carry their own air so they can breathe inside smoky buildings.

questions.ask: A fireproof uniform and helmet
questions.fact: Their special kit protects firefighters from heat and flames.

questions.ask: A camera that sees through smoke
questions.fact: A thermal camera shows warm things, so firefighters can find people in thick smoke.

quests.title: Mr Pepys's Diary

skill.name: The Great Fire of London in order
skill.subject: history

quests.story: Oh no, Mr Pepys has dropped his diary and the pages are muddled! Help him put the story of the fire back in order.
quests.instruction: Tap the event that happened first in Mr Pepys's story.
quests.hint: First the fire started, then it spread, then it stopped, and last of all London was rebuilt.

events.label: Pepys starts a diary
events.fact: Samuel Pepys began his diary on 1 January 1660 and wrote in it almost every day.

events.label: Fire starts in bakery
events.fact: The fire began in the early hours of Sunday morning in Thomas Farriner's bakery.

events.label: Pepys tells the King
events.fact: Pepys took a boat to Whitehall Palace to tell King Charles II how bad the fire was.

events.label: St Paul's burns down
events.fact: The old St Paul's Cathedral burned on the fourth day of the fire.

events.label: The fire goes out
events.fact: The wind dropped, and by 6 September the fire was almost all out.

events.label: Wren draws new plans
events.fact: Christopher Wren drew a plan for a new London with wide streets.

events.label: New homes of brick
events.fact: A new law said houses must be built of brick or stone, not wood.

events.label: Pepys ends his diary
events.fact: Pepys stopped writing because he was worried about his eyesight.

events.label: The Monument is built
events.fact: The Monument took six years to build and you can climb 311 steps to the top.

events.label: New St Paul's is done
events.fact: Wren's new St Paul's Cathedral, with its huge dome, took over 35 years to build.

quests.title: One Small Step
quests.story: 3, 2, 1, blast off! Zoom to the Moon and find out about the very first people to walk on it.
quests.instruction: Read each question about the Moon landing, then tap the answer.
quests.hint: Think about the Apollo 11 crew and their trip in 1969. Who did what?

questions.ask: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969.

questions.ask: In what year did people land on the Moon?
questions.fact: No one had ever stood on another world before.

questions.ask: Who was the second person on the Moon?
questions.fact: Buzz Aldrin followed Neil down the ladder about 20 minutes later.

questions.ask: Who stayed flying around the Moon?
questions.fact: Michael Collins flew the command module, ready to take the crew home.

questions.ask: What was the mission called?
questions.fact: Apollo was the name of a Greek god, and this was the 11th Apollo mission.

questions.ask: What was the landing craft called?
questions.fact: When it landed, Neil said, "The Eagle has landed."

questions.ask: Which giant rocket blasted them off?
questions.fact: Saturn V was taller than Big Ben's tower and very, very loud.

questions.ask: Which country sent them to the Moon?
questions.fact: The mission was run by NASA, the American space agency.

questions.ask: What did they put up on the Moon?
questions.fact: They also left a sign that said they came in peace for all people.

questions.ask: What did they bring back to Earth?
questions.fact: They collected about 22 kilograms of rock and dust for scientists to study.

questions.ask: How did people at home watch the landing?
questions.fact: About 600 million people watched the fuzzy black-and-white pictures live.

questions.ask: Finish Neil's words: One small step for…?
questions.fact: He went on: "…one giant leap for mankind."

quests.title: Up, Up and Away!
quests.story: Whoosh! On windy sand dunes, two brothers are about to fly a plane for the very first time. Join them!
quests.instruction: Read each question about the first flight, then tap the answer.
quests.hint: Think about the two brothers from America and their short, wobbly first flight in 1903.

questions.ask: Who made the first powered plane flight?
questions.fact: Before planes, people could only fly in balloons and gliders.

questions.ask: What were the two brothers called?
questions.fact: Wilbur was the older brother, and Orville was four years younger.

questions.ask: In what year was the first flight?
questions.fact: The first flight was on a cold, windy day: 17 December 1903.

questions.ask: Where did they fly?
questions.fact: The windy sand dunes near Kitty Hawk, in the USA, were good for flying and soft landings.

questions.ask: What was their plane called?
questions.fact: The Flyer was made of wood and cloth, with two long wings.

questions.ask: How long did the first flight last?
questions.fact: In 12 seconds the plane flew about 37 metres, less than a jumbo jet's length.

questions.ask: What kind of shop did the brothers run?
questions.fact: Fixing bikes taught them a lot about balance and building machines.

questions.ask: Which brother flew first?
questions.fact: The brothers tossed a coin to choose, and Wilbur won, but his first try failed.

questions.ask: What toy gave them the idea of flying?
questions.fact: Their dad gave them a little flying toy powered by a rubber band.

questions.ask: What made the plane go?
questions.fact: They built a light petrol engine with their mechanic, Charlie Taylor.

questions.ask: How did the pilot ride the Flyer?
questions.fact: The pilot lay flat on his tummy on the bottom wing.

questions.ask: How many flights did they make that day?
questions.fact: The longest of the four flights that day lasted 59 seconds.

quests.title: Nurses of the Crimea
quests.story: Two brave women helped soldiers in the Crimean War. Find out how Florence Nightingale and Mary Seacole each helped.
quests.instruction: Is it about Florence or about Mary? Tap the right basket.
quests.hint: Florence ran a big army hospital. Mary came from Jamaica and set up her own place to help.

questions.ask: Born in the city of Florence, Italy
questions.fact: Her parents named her after the city where she was born in 1820.

questions.ask: Ran the army hospital at Scutari
questions.fact: The British government asked her to take charge of the nurses there.

questions.ask: Called the Lady with the Lamp
questions.fact: She walked the wards at night with a lamp to check on the soldiers.

questions.ask: Made clever charts with numbers
questions.fact: Her charts helped show that clean hospitals saved lives.

questions.ask: Started a nursing school in London
questions.fact: Her school opened in 1860 at St Thomas' Hospital.

questions.ask: Took 38 nurses to the war
questions.fact: She set off with her team of nurses in 1854.

questions.ask: Born in Kingston, Jamaica
questions.fact: Mary was born in 1805. Her mother was Jamaican and her father was Scottish.

questions.ask: Used herbal remedies
questions.fact: Mary learned to make medicines from plants from her mother, who was a healer.

questions.ask: Built the British Hotel
questions.fact: Near Balaclava she opened a place where soldiers could get food, rest and care.

questions.ask: Paid her own way to the war
questions.fact: When she was not chosen to go, Mary travelled to the Crimea with her own money.

questions.ask: Called Mother Seacole by soldiers
questions.fact: The soldiers loved her kindness and her good food.

questions.ask: Wrote Wonderful Adventures
questions.fact: Her book about her life came out in 1857 and sold many copies.

quests.title: Remember, Remember
quests.story: Shh! Creep down into the dark cellar under Parliament and uncover the secret plot of 1605.
quests.instruction: Read each question about the plot, then tap the right answer.
quests.hint: Think about the plotters, the King, and the secret letter that gave the plan away.

questions.ask: On what date was the plot found out?
questions.fact: That is why Bonfire Night is on 5 November every year.

questions.ask: In what year was the Gunpowder Plot?
questions.fact: The plot was over 400 years ago, in the time of the Stuart kings.

questions.ask: Who was caught guarding the gunpowder?
questions.fact: Guy Fawkes knew a lot about gunpowder from his time as a soldier.

questions.ask: Who was the king in 1605?
questions.fact: James was already King of Scotland when he became King of England too.

questions.ask: What did the plotters want to blow up?
questions.fact: The plotters were Catholics who were angry about harsh laws against them.

questions.ask: Where was the gunpowder hidden?
questions.fact: It was under the House of Lords, covered with piles of firewood.

questions.ask: Who was the leader of the plot?
questions.fact: Robert Catesby planned the plot and asked others to join him.

questions.ask: What gave the secret plan away?
questions.fact: A letter warned Lord Monteagle to stay away from Parliament, and he told the King's men.

questions.ask: How many barrels of gunpowder were there?
questions.fact: That was enough gunpowder to destroy the whole building.

questions.ask: What do people light on 5 November?
questions.fact: People lit bonfires in 1605 to celebrate that the King was safe.

questions.ask: What lights up the sky on Bonfire Night?
questions.fact: Fireworks remind us of the gunpowder that never went off.

questions.ask: Who still searches Parliament's cellars?
questions.fact: Before the State Opening of Parliament, the Yeomen of the Guard search the cellars.

quests.title: Brave Explorers
quests.story: One explorer sailed across the sea and one flew to the Moon! Sort the clues to find out which explorer each one is about.
quests.instruction: Is it about Columbus or Neil Armstrong? Tap the right chest.
quests.hint: Columbus sailed in 1492 with ships and wind. Neil flew in 1969 with a rocket.

questions.ask: Set sail in 1492
questions.fact: Christopher Columbus was from Genoa in Italy, but his trip was paid for by Spain.

questions.ask: Took three ships
questions.fact: His three ships were the Niña, the Pinta and the Santa María.

questions.ask: Led the ship Santa María
questions.fact: The Santa María was the biggest of his three wooden ships.

questions.ask: Set off from Spain
questions.fact: He sailed west across the Atlantic Ocean for over two months.

questions.ask: Thought he had reached Asia
questions.fact: He had really reached islands in the Caribbean, where people already lived.

questions.ask: Used the wind and stars to travel
questions.fact: Sailors used the stars and a compass to find their way across the sea.

questions.ask: Flew into space in 1969
questions.fact: Neil Armstrong was an American pilot and astronaut.

questions.ask: Travelled in a giant rocket
questions.fact: The Saturn V rocket took three days to reach the Moon.

questions.ask: First to walk on the Moon
questions.fact: His footprints are still there, because there is no wind on the Moon.

questions.ask: Wore a spacesuit and helmet
questions.fact: The spacesuit gave him air to breathe and kept him safe from heat and cold.

questions.ask: Talked to Earth by radio
questions.fact: Mission Control in Houston, USA, could hear him from the Moon.

questions.ask: Landed in a craft called Eagle
questions.fact: Neil steered the Eagle past big rocks to find a safe landing place.

quests.title: Two Queens

skill.name: Queen Victoria and Queen Elizabeth II
skill.subject: history

quests.story: Two famous queens have left their crowns in the castle! Sort the clues to find out which queen each one is about.
quests.instruction: Is it about Queen Victoria or Elizabeth II? Tap the right shield.
quests.hint: Victoria lived in the 1800s, before TV. Elizabeth II lived much closer to our time.

questions.ask: Became queen in 1837
questions.fact: Victoria was just 18 years old when she became queen.

questions.ask: Married Prince Albert
questions.fact: Prince Albert helped to bring the Christmas tree tradition to Britain.

questions.ask: Had nine children
questions.fact: Her children married into royal families all over Europe.

questions.ask: Was Empress of India
questions.fact: She was given this title in 1876, when Britain ruled India.

questions.ask: Wore black for 40 years
questions.fact: She wore black for the rest of her life after Albert died in 1861.

questions.ask: Took her first train ride in 1842
questions.fact: Railways spread all over Britain while Victoria was queen.

questions.ask: Crowned in 1953
questions.fact: Her coronation was shown on TV, and many families bought a TV to watch it.

questions.ask: Married Prince Philip
questions.fact: They were married for 73 years.

questions.ask: Loved her corgi dogs
questions.fact: She had more than 30 corgis during her life.

questions.ask: Was queen for 70 years
questions.fact: She reigned longer than any other British king or queen, even Victoria.

questions.ask: Had a Platinum Jubilee
questions.fact: In 2022 people held street parties to celebrate her 70 years as queen.

questions.ask: Sent her first email in 1976
questions.fact: She was one of the first heads of state to send an email.

quests.title: The Great Museum Timeline
quests.story: The museum's timeline has fallen down! Help the curator put famous events from history back in the right order.
quests.instruction: Tap the event in the museum that happened first.
quests.hint: Ships and sails came long before planes, and rockets and computers came last of all. Look for clues!

events.label: Columbus sets sail
events.fact: Columbus crossed the Atlantic Ocean with three wooden sailing ships.

events.label: Gunpowder Plot
events.fact: Guy Fawkes was caught in the cellar under Parliament on 5 November.

events.label: Great Fire of London
events.fact: The fire started in a bakery on Pudding Lane and burned for about four days.

events.label: Grace Darling rescue
events.fact: Grace and her dad rowed through a storm to save nine people.

events.label: Florence at Scutari
events.fact: Florence Nightingale made the army hospital clean and safe.

events.label: First powered flight
events.fact: The Wright brothers flew for 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk, USA.

events.label: Elizabeth II crowned
events.fact: Millions of people watched the coronation on television.

events.label: First person in space
events.fact: Yuri Gagarin from the Soviet Union flew once around the Earth.

events.label: Moon landing
events.fact: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon.

events.label: First web page
events.fact: Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist, invented the World Wide Web.
